page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-2g is a specialized accelerator-optimized instance built around dual NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs delivering a combined 80 GB of VRAM. Compute processing is driven by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, allocated as 24 dedicated virtual CPUs across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 170.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.08 GB per vCPU, backed by 38 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring persistent network-attached storage volumes for file systems and runtime data.

Benchmark results highlight clear performance divergence between general compute and GPU-accelerated processing. Single-core performance falls into the lower 25 percent bracket across benchmarks such as stress-ng, Geekbench, and compression suites, reflecting the moderate 2.2 GHz base clock frequency. Multi-core operations register in the middle 50 percent category, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 19022.15 and a multi-threaded bzip3 throughput of 63.75 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth scales up to 1055.63 GB/sec under small cached blocks and maintains 106.77 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The primary strength of the instance is deep learning inference and high-throughput tensor operations. Across large language model benchmarks, the two A100 GPUs achieve top-decile prompt processing throughput, generating 2823.17 tokens per second on 7B models and 498.53 tokens per second on 70B models. Text generation maintains top-tier speeds of 130.58 tokens per second on 7B architectures and 22.39 tokens per second on 70B models.

Given its architecture, the a2-highgpu-2g represents a dedicated platform for machine learning inference, distributed neural network training, computer vision models, and GPU-centric high-performance computing pipelines. It is less suited for serial CPU-bound tasks or disk-intensive operations without external high-throughput storage attachments.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-2g is an accelerator-optimized instance configured with two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing 80 GB of total VRAM, 24 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (12 physical cores) running at 2.2 GHz, and 170.0 GB of system memory. It does not bundle local disk storage and includes zero default public IPv4 addresses. While CPU benchmarks reflect bottom-quartile single-core metrics and middle-tier multi-core results, the dual A100 GPUs place the server in the top 10 percent for large language model inference, achieving 2823.17 tokens per second during 7B model prompt processing and sustained generation throughput on 70B models. System memory bandwidth reaches 106.77 GB/sec on uncached reads. This configuration represents an efficient resource allocation for distributed deep learning, LLM serving, and GPU-accelerated scientific computing workloads.
